title: A finite filtration with injective graded pieces admits a compatible splitting
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be an abelian category [def-sp-abelian], let $a\le b$ be integers, and let $(I,F)$ have a decreasing filtration [def-sp-filtration] with $F^aI=I$ and $F^{b+1}I=0$. Suppose that $\operatorname{gr}^n I=F^nI/F^{n+1}I$ is injective in the extension-property sense of [def-sp-injective-resolutions] for every $a\le n\le b$. There exist injective objects $J_n$ for $a\le n\le b$, isomorphisms $J_n\cong\operatorname{gr}^n I$, and an isomorphism $\theta:I\xrightarrow{\sim}\bigoplus_{n=a}^b J_n$ identifying $F^pI$ with the sub-biproduct $\bigoplus_{a\le n\le b,\ n\ge p}J_n$ for every integer $p$.

source.place: Tag 05TP, lemma-filtered-injective; the specified interval and identification of J_n with gr^n I follow from its displayed split filtration

proof.text: Put $J_n=\operatorname{gr}^n I$ for $a\le n\le b$, so these objects are injective by hypothesis and their required graded-piece isomorphisms are identities. For $a\le n\le b+1$ put $B_n=\bigoplus_{n\le k\le b}J_k$; these finite biproducts exist by [def-sp-abelian]. Write $u_{p,n}:F^pI\to F^nI$ for the filtration inclusion and $j_{p,n}:B_p\to B_n$ for the tail inclusion when $n\le p\le b+1$. Construct, by induction on the nonnegative integer $b+1-n$, isomorphisms $\theta_n:F^nI\xrightarrow{\sim}B_n$ satisfying $\theta_n u_{p,n}=j_{p,n}\theta_p$ for every $n\le p\le b+1$. The base $n=b+1$ is the unique isomorphism from $F^{b+1}I=0$ to the empty biproduct $B_{b+1}=0$; its sole compatibility equation is the identity.

source.place: Tag 05TP, lemma-filtered-injective: expand the omitted finite-filtration splitting argument

proof.text: Suppose the compatible isomorphisms have been constructed for indices $n+1,\ldots,b+1$, where $a\le n\le b$. The biproduct $B_{n+1}$ is also the product of the finite family $(J_k)_{n+1\le k\le b}$. By [lem-weil-pbc-product-injectives] it is injective, including when this family is empty. Consequently $F^{n+1}I$ is injective: for a monomorphism $v:M\to N$ and a map $f:M\to F^{n+1}I$, extend $\theta_{n+1}f$ to $g:N\to B_{n+1}$ and then use $\theta_{n+1}^{-1}g$ as the extension of $f$. This verifies exactly the extension property of [def-sp-injective-resolutions].

source.place: Tag 0137, lemma-product-injectives; applied to finite biproducts in the induction for derived.tex Tag 05TP

proof.text: Let $i_n=u_{n+1,n}$ and let $q_n:F^nI\to J_n=F^nI/F^{n+1}I$ be the quotient. By the definition of a subobject quotient in an abelian category, $i_n$ is the kernel of $q_n$, $q_n$ is its cokernel, and hence $0\to F^{n+1}I\xrightarrow{i_n}F^nI\xrightarrow{q_n}J_n\to0$ is short exact. The first object is injective by Step 2, so [lem-weil-pbc-ses-injective-kernel-splits] gives $r_n:F^nI\to F^{n+1}I$ and $s_n:J_n\to F^nI$ with $r_ni_n=1$, $q_ns_n=1$, and $i_nr_n+s_nq_n=1$. It is the injectivity of the first term, established by descending induction, that permits this application.

source.place: Tag 0136, lemma-characterize-injectives, (1) implies (3); the injection-splitting fact used by derived.tex Tag 05TP

proof.text: The splitting identities also give $r_ns_n=0$: composing $i_nr_n+s_nq_n=1$ with $s_n$ yields $i_nr_ns_n=0$, and $i_n$ is monic. Therefore the maps $(q_n,r_n):F^nI\to J_n\oplus F^{n+1}I$ and $(s_n,i_n):J_n\oplus F^{n+1}I\to F^nI$ are inverse: the composite on $F^nI$ is $s_nq_n+i_nr_n=1$, and the four blocks of the other composite are $q_ns_n=1$, $q_ni_n=0$, $r_ns_n=0$, $r_ni_n=1$. Compose the first isomorphism with $1_{J_n}\oplus\theta_{n+1}$ and identify $J_n\oplus B_{n+1}$ with $B_n$, using the same coordinates indexed by $k=n,\ldots,b$. This defines $\theta_n$.

source.place: Tag 05TP, lemma-filtered-injective: expand the omitted finite-filtration splitting argument

proof.text: Since $q_ni_n=0$ and $r_ni_n=1$, the just-constructed map satisfies $\theta_ni_n=j_{n+1,n}\theta_{n+1}$. If $n+1\le p\le b+1$, the inclusions satisfy $u_{p,n}=i_nu_{p,n+1}$, so the induction hypothesis gives $\theta_nu_{p,n}=j_{n+1,n}\theta_{n+1}u_{p,n+1}=j_{n+1,n}j_{p,n+1}\theta_p=j_{p,n}\theta_p$. For $p=n$ the equation is the identity. Thus the whole compatibility invariant is preserved. All equations here are equations of morphisms; as $\theta_p$ is an isomorphism, they identify the subobject $F^pI\subseteq F^nI$ with precisely the tail sub-biproduct $B_p\subseteq B_n$.

source.place: Tag 05TP, lemma-filtered-injective: expand the omitted finite-filtration splitting argument

proof.text: After the finite descent to $n=a$, use $F^aI=I$ to set $\theta=\theta_a:I\xrightarrow{\sim}\bigoplus_{k=a}^bJ_k$. Step 5 proves the required subobject identification for $a\le p\le b+1$. For $p<a$, decreasingness gives $I=F^aI\subseteq F^pI\subseteq I$, so $F^pI=I$ and every index $k\in[a,b]$ satisfies $k\ge p$. For $p>b+1$, decreasingness gives $F^pI\subseteq F^{b+1}I=0$, while the specified index set is empty. Hence the same $\theta$ works for every integer $p$, with the injective $J_n$ and their identity graded-piece isomorphisms chosen in Step 1.
